newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aer Lingus renews France cargo contract.
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus renews France cargo contract.

text.p: PARIS, May 2 - Irish airline Aer Lingus said it had extended its cargo handling contract with French operator Societe de Fret de Services (SFS) for a further two years.

"Although our policy is to award handling contracts on a yearly basis, we had no hesitation in extending the arrangement with SFS for two years," Pat Maguire, strategy manager of Aer Lingus Cargo, said in a statement.
He also said the airline was expanding co-operation between the two companies by adding the handler's trucking service to its own range of cargo products.

"We will now be able to offer our customers, both in Ireland and France, a destination-to-destination service on a fixed tariff basis. There is considerable potential for developing this facility due to booming trade between France and Ireland," said Maguire."

Aer Lingus operates four daily flights between Paris and Dublin using Boeing 737 aircraft, which carry an average of 1.3 tonnes of freight, the carrier's French cargo sales agent, Transport Assistance Service (TAS), told Reuters.
"With four daily flights to Dublin, we can offer a great deal of flexibility for small-volume shipments, particularly those in the express category," a TAS official said.
Ex-France shipments on the route comprise mainly luxury goods -- fashion wear, perfumes and cosmetics -- for the Irish market.

In the return direction, there was expanded trade in manufactured goods such as electrical and electronic parts and components as a result of the influx of multi-national companies in Ireland, SFS said.
Many of these products were transported by air due to their high value-to-weight ratio and urgency, SFS said.
Aer Lingus also operates daily Paris-Cork and weekly Paris-Shannon services.
